title: Why multitasking actually makes you less productive
hook: Still struggling to finish multiple tasks at once?

narration.text: Your brain cannot truly multitask, it just switches rapidly between tasks.
This switching comes with a hidden cost, called 'attention residue'.
Each time you switch, a part of your attention stays on the previous task.
This makes it harder to focus fully on the new task at hand.
It means every interruption, like a notification, slows down your progress.
Focusing on one task until completion boosts both speed and accuracy.
Do you find yourself constantly switching tasks throughout your day?

description: Discover why trying to do too many things at once often backfires. We explain the concept of attention switching costs and how it impacts your daily productivity. Learn how focusing on one task can actually make you more efficient.
topic: Why multitasking is often less efficient than focusing on one task, explaining attention switching costs.
